saints.name: St. Bernardine of Siena
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: The Franciscan preacher who carried the Holy Name of Jesus across Italy on his famous tablet…
biography: Bernardino degli Albizzeschi was born of a noble Sienese family at Massa Marittima on 8 September 1380 and orphaned at six. When plague struck Siena in 1400 he took charge of the hospital of Santa Maria della Scala for four months; in 1402 he entered the Observant Franciscans and was ordained priest in 1404.

For more than thirty years he travelled Italy on foot, drawing crowds so great that pulpits were set up in the marketplaces, preaching against usury, faction, and gambling until his hearers burned cards and dice in bonfires of the vanities. Above all he spread devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus, holding up a tablet bearing the monogram IHS on a blazing sun to displace the badges of the factions.

Summoned to Rome in 1426 to answer for this devotion, he was acquitted and preached there daily for eighty days. He refused the bishoprics of Siena, Ferrara, and Urbino, and as vicar-general from 1438 raised the Observants from 130 friars to over 4,000. He died at L'Aquila on 20 May 1444 and was canonized by Nicholas V in 1450. From his emblem comes his patronage of advertisers.
saints.knownFor: Preaching the Holy Name of Jesus across Italy.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 20 May
